paragraphs.source_en: Whenever Ieyasu saw Shigemasa, he would say, “My efforts are still not enough.” Whenever a decision had to be made, he summoned elders of the Five Mountains or monks from Mount Koya and listened to their views. paragraphs.source_en: On the fifteenth day of the sixth month in the twentieth year of Keicho, Ieyasu once again entered the palace for an audience with the sovereign. He reported that he had sent men to clear the burned ruins of Osaka Castle, that a castle under the shogunate’s direct control would be built upon its former foundations, and that all the nearby roads would be repaired to foster prosperity throughout the Kinai region. Finally, he presented one thousand ryo of silver, two hundred bolts of brocade, and other gifts.

paragraphs.source_en: The restoration of Osaka Castle and the pursuit and killing of the defeated warriors were both conducted under Shogun Hidetada’s command.
